title: Cell signaling by receptor tyrosine kinases
why: Single best backbone reference: systematizes activation modes across all 58 human RTKs, so the receptor layer's node types and activation-edge semantics can be derived from one source rather than stitched from subfamily papers.
authors: Lemmon MA, Schlessinger J.

title: Untangling the ErbB signalling network
why: Provides an essentially pre-built subgraph — 4 receptors x ~11 ligands -> specific homo/heterodimers -> distinct outputs — including the asymmetry rules (HER2 ligandless, HER3 kinase-dead) that make ErbB edges partner-dependent.
authors: Yarden Y, Sliwkowski MX.

title: An allosteric mechanism for activation of the kinase domain of epidermal growth factor receptor
why: The asymmetric activator/receiver kinase dimer is the mechanistic reason EGFR/ErbB activation edges must be directional between partners rather than a symmetric dimerization relation.
authors: Zhang X, Gureasko J, Shen K, Cole PA, Kuriyan J.

title: The SH2 and SH3 domain-containing protein GRB2 links receptor tyrosine kinases to ras signaling
why: Founding evidence for the prototype receptor -> pTyr -> SH2 adaptor -> GEF -> small GTPase chain that the entire adaptor-recruitment layer of the KG is modelled on.
authors: Lowenstein EJ, Daly RJ, Batzer AG, Li W, Margolis B, Lammers R, Ullrich A, Skolnik EY, Bar-Sagi D, Schlessinger J.

title: Specificity of receptor tyrosine kinase signaling: transient versus sustained extracellular signal-regulated kinase activation
why: The origin evidence that an identical ERK node yields opposite phenotypes depending on activation duration, forcing stimulus->phenotype paths in the KG to carry a temporal qualifier rather than a binary activation flag.
authors: Marshall CJ.

title: A quantitative protein interaction network for the ErbB receptors using protein microarrays
why: Directly ingestible affinity-quantified matrix of ErbB pTyr sites against SH2/PTB domains — turns receptor->adaptor links from binary edges into site-resolved weighted ones.
authors: Jones RB, Gordus A, Krall JA, MacBeath G.

title: Crystal structure of a ternary FGF-FGFR-heparin complex reveals a dual role for heparin in FGFR binding and dimerization
why: Establishes an obligatory co-receptor (heparan sulfate) node in the ligand->receptor edge, the clearest counterexample to the generic two-ligand-two-receptor dimerization rule inherited from EGFR.
authors: Schlessinger J, Plotnikov AN, Ibrahimi OA, Eliseenkova AV, Yeh BK, Yayon A, Linhardt RJ, Mohammadi M.

title: Biochemical and cellular properties of insulin receptor signalling
why: Covers the one RTK topology the EGFR-centric literature does not — a pre-formed disulfide-linked dimer routing through IRS scaffolds to PI3K-AKT and compartment-specific metabolic phenotypes.
authors: Haeusler RA, McGraw TE, Accili D.

title: Crystal structure of the β2 adrenergic receptor-Gs protein complex
why: The canonical structural definition of the agonist-receptor→nucleotide-free-Gs edge, fixing what 'coupling' physically means for every receptor→G-protein relation in the KG.
authors: Rasmussen SG, DeVree BT, Zou Y, Kruse AC, Chung KY, Kobilka TS, Thian FS, Chae PS, Pardon E, Calinski D, Mathiesen JM, Shah ST, Lyons JA, Caffrey M, Gellman SH, Steyaert J, Skiniotis G, Weis WI, Sunahara RK, Kobilka BK.

title: The Molecular Basis of G Protein-Coupled Receptor Activation
why: Weis/Kobilka's synthesis of receptor conformational ensembles and activation energetics gives the mechanistic justification for treating a receptor node as a multi-state entity rather than an on/off switch.
authors: Weis WI, Kobilka BK.

title: Illuminating G-Protein-Coupling Selectivity of GPCRs
why: Systematic Gα-chimera screen across ~150 receptors yields a directly ingestible receptor→Gs/Gi/Gq/G12-13 coupling matrix — the single best quantitative source for populating coupling edges.

title: Effector membrane translocation biosensors reveal G protein and βarrestin coupling profiles of 100 therapeutically relevant GPCRs
why: Orthogonal BRET transducerome map covering all G proteins plus β-arrestins for 100 receptors, the cross-validation set that keeps coupling edges from resting on a single assay platform.

title: Biased signalling: from simple switches to allosteric microprocessors
why: Definitive framing of ligand-dependent transducer routing, i.e. why receptor→transducer edges must be conditioned on the ligand rather than stored as fixed pathway membership.
authors: Smith JS, Lefkowitz RJ, Rajagopal S.

title: Identification of Phosphorylation Codes for Arrestin Recruitment by G Protein-Coupled Receptors
why: Turns the receptor phospho-barcode into explicit sequence rules (PxPP/PxxPxxP) that predict arrestin recruitment, making GRK→receptor-phosphosite→arrestin edges derivable rather than curated case-by-case.
authors: Zhou XE, He Y, de Waal PW, Gao X, Kang Y, Van Eps N, Yin Y, Pal K, Goswami D, White TA, Barty A, Latorraca NR, Chapman HN, Hubbell WL, Dror RO, Stevens RC, Cherezov V, Gurevich VV, Griffin PR, Ernst OP, Melcher K, Xu HE.

title: Subcellular Organization of the cAMP Signaling Pathway
why: The one modern synthesis that assembles AC isoforms, PDE-defined sinks, AKAP scaffolds and biosensor evidence into an explicitly compartmentalized cAMP map, making it the scaffold on which every location-resolved cAMP/PKA edge can be built.
authors: Zaccolo M, Zerio A, Lobo MJ.

title: Mechanisms of Vascular Smooth Muscle Contraction and the Basis for Pharmacologic Treatment of Smooth Muscle Disorders
why: The one candidate that traces the G12-13→RhoGEF→RhoA/ROCK and Gq→Ca2+/MLCK arms all the way to a measurable phenotype, anchoring the otherwise dangling effector→phenotype terminus.
authors: Brozovich FV, Nicholson CJ, Degen CV, Gao YZ, Aggarwal M, Morgan KG.

title: Activation and function of the MAPKs and their substrates, the MAPK-activated protein kinases
journal: Microbiology and molecular biology reviews : MMBR
why: Single most complete source for the three-tier module wiring of ERK/JNK/p38 plus the MAPKAPK effector layer (RSK, MSK, MNK, MK2/3/5), so it can be mined directly for kinase->substrate->effector edges across all arms; it supersedes the narrower 2004 MMBR RSK/MSK/MNK review also in the list.
authors: Cargnello M, Roux PP.

title: RAS Proteins and Their Regulators in Human Disease
why: Authoritative Cell catalogue of RAS isoforms, GEFs, GAPs, effectors and their mutational states — the definitive node/edge inventory for the receptor->GTPase interface that feeds RAF, making the 2023 Biochem J RAS review redundant.
authors: Simanshu DK, Nissley DV, McCormick F.

title: RAF inhibitors transactivate RAF dimers and ERK signalling in cells with wild-type BRAF
why: Landmark proof that RAF signals as an obligate dimer with occupancy-dependent transactivation, forcing the KG to model the RAS->RAF->MEK edge as a non-additive, allosteric complex rather than a linear activation arrow.
authors: Poulikakos PI, Zhang C, Bollag G, Shokat KM, Rosen N.

title: Ultrasensitivity in the mitogen-activated protein kinase cascade
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
why: Huang-Ferrell established that dual phosphorylation across three tiers yields switch-like ultrasensitivity (Hill ~4-5), which is the quantitative reason cascade edges must carry nonlinear transfer semantics instead of proportional weights.
authors: Huang CY, Ferrell JE.

title: Using optogenetics to interrogate the dynamic control of signal transmission by the Ras/Erk module
why: Method paper that made input-output dynamics of the cascade directly measurable, yielding the fast, low-pass transfer function between Ras and Erk that parameterises every temporal-encoding edge in the KG.
authors: Toettcher JE, Weiner OD, Lim WA.

title: Scaffold proteins: hubs for controlling the flow of cellular information
why: Gives the information-flow vocabulary — insulation, tethered feedback, allosteric modulation — needed to type scaffold nodes and their modulatory edges, replacing both the 1997 adaptor typology and the MAPK-scaffold review.
authors: Good MC, Zalatan JG, Lim WA.

title: Negative feedback regulation of the ERK1/2 MAPK pathway
journal: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS
why: The most complete site-level inventory of ERK negative-feedback edges (SOS1, RAF S289/296/301, MEK T292, SPRY/SPRED, DUSPs), i.e. the concrete edge list needed to instantiate the feedback subgraph that shapes ERK amplitude and duration.
authors: Lake D, Corrêa SA, Müller J.

title: JNK Signaling: Regulation and Functions Based on Complex Protein-Protein Partnerships
journal: Microbiology and molecular biology reviews : MMBR
why: Comprehensive MAP3K->MKK4/7->JNK module map with JIP scaffolding and substrate partnerships, giving the stress-MAPK arm the same node/edge resolution the ERK arm gets elsewhere in this set.
authors: Zeke A, Misheva M, Reményi A, Bogoyevitch MA.

title: Cell-signalling dynamics in time and space
why: Kholodenko's synthesis of how feedback loops, oscillations and spatial gradients convert MAPK topology into temporal codes — the design rationale for attaching dynamic and spatial attributes to cascade edges at all.
authors: Kholodenko BN.

title: mTOR at the nexus of nutrition, growth, ageing and disease
why: Single most complete authoritative synthesis of how amino-acid, growth-factor and energy inputs converge on lysosomal mTORC1 (and mTORC2), giving the backbone node/edge inventory for the entire mTOR half of this layer.
authors: Liu GY, Sabatini DM.

title: AKT/PKB Signaling: Navigating the Network
why: Curated, motif-annotated catalogue of validated AKT substrates (TSC2, PRAS40, FOXO, GSK3, AS160) with isoform/context caveats — the most directly ingestible source of kinase->substrate edges in this domain.
authors: Manning BD, Toker A.

title: The PI3K Pathway in Human Disease
why: Defines the upstream entry edges of the pathway — class I PI3K isoform usage, RTK vs GPCR vs RAS coupling, and p85 regulatory control — which no downstream AKT/mTOR review supplies.
authors: Fruman DA, Chiu H, Hopkins BD, Bagrodia S, Cantley LC, Abraham RT.

title: The tumor suppressor, PTEN/MMAC1, dephosphorylates the lipid second messenger, phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate
why: Landmark that established PTEN as the PIP3 3-phosphatase, supplying the one canonical negative-regulator edge that makes the PIP3 node dynamic rather than a one-way switch.
authors: Maehama T, Dixon JE.

title: TSC2 is phosphorylated and inhibited by Akt and suppresses mTOR signalling
why: The primary evidence for the AKT->TSC2 inhibitory phosphorylation that is the load-bearing link joining the PI3K/AKT arm to the mTORC1 arm of the graph.
authors: Inoki K, Li Y, Zhu T, Wu J, Guan KL.

title: Phosphorylation and regulation of Akt/PKB by the rictor-mTOR complex
why: Identifies mTORC2 as the AKT Ser473 hydrophobic-motif kinase, defining mTORC2 as a separate node and creating the mTOR->AKT feedback edge that makes the network cyclic.
authors: Sarbassov DD, Guertin DA, Ali SM, Sabatini DM.

title: Ragulator-Rag complex targets mTORC1 to the lysosomal surface and is necessary for its activation by amino acids
why: Establishes that amino-acid signalling works by physically relocating mTORC1 to the lysosome via Rag-Ragulator — the single best justification for attaching a compartment attribute to signalling edges, and the anchor for the whole nutrient-sensor subgraph.
authors: Sancak Y, Bar-Peled L, Zoncu R, Markhard AL, Nada S, Sabatini DM.

title: Akt promotes cell survival by phosphorylating and inhibiting a Forkhead transcription factor
why: Canonical primary source for the AKT->FOXO phosphorylation -> 14-3-3 -> nuclear exclusion -> survival chain, i.e. the domain's cleanest kinase->TF->localization->phenotype path.
authors: Brunet A, Bonni A, Zigmond MJ, Lin MZ, Juo P, Hu LS, Anderson MJ, Arden KC, Blenis J, Greenberg ME.

title: Jak-STAT pathways and transcriptional activation in response to IFNs and other extracellular signaling proteins
why: The paper that defined the ligand->receptor->JAK->STAT->GAS-element edge chain, so it is the canonical schema reference the KG's JAK-STAT backbone should be typed against.
authors: Darnell JE, Kerr IM, Stark GR.

title: The JAK-STAT pathway at 30: Much learned, much more to do
why: Written by the pathway's founders as a current status report, it is the single best source for marking which JAK-STAT edges are settled versus contested when assigning evidence-layer confidence (and it supersedes the 1994 and 2012 retrospectives for current wiring).
authors: Philips RL, Wang Y, Cheon H, Kanno Y, Gadina M, Sartorelli V, Horvath CM, Darnell JE, Stark GR, O'Shea JJ.

title: Mechanisms and consequences of Jak-STAT signaling in the immune system
why: Provides the explicit cytokine-receptor -> JAK-pair -> STAT-set assignment tables plus the chromatin output, which is the most directly transcribable source for populating receptor_kinase triples across the cytokine families.
authors: Villarino AV, Kanno Y, O'Shea JJ.

title: Structure of a Janus kinase cytokine receptor complex reveals the basis for dimeric activation
why: The cryo-EM structure of the JAK-bound receptor dimer gives the physical, stoichiometry-resolved definition of the receptor->JAK coupling edge and of how dimerization licenses trans-phosphorylation, superseding the earlier piecemeal interface and pseudokinase structures in this list.
authors: Glassman CR, Tsutsumi N, Saxton RA, Lupardus PJ, Jude KM, Garcia KC.

title: Crystal structure of a tyrosine phosphorylated STAT-1 dimer bound to DNA
why: Structural proof that reciprocal SH2-pTyr701 docking is what converts STAT phosphorylation into a DNA-binding dimer, i.e. the mechanistic justification for modelling phospho-STAT, STAT dimer and STAT-DNA as three distinct KG states rather than one.
authors: Chen X, Vinkemeier U, Zhao Y, Jeruzalmi D, Darnell JE, Kuriyan J.

title: SOCS proteins, cytokine signalling and immune regulation
why: The definitive mapping of which cytokine induces which SOCS and which JAK/receptor that SOCS shuts down, giving the complete cytokine->SOCS->target negative-feedback loop set in one ingestible reference (covers the SOCS-box, gp130-Y757 and SOCS1-knockout primary papers also proposed).
authors: Yoshimura A, Naka T, Kubo M.

title: Regulation of type I interferon responses
why: Supplies the whole IFNAR1/2 -> TYK2/JAK1 -> STAT1/STAT2/IRF9 (ISGF3) sub-graph together with its tuning and cross-talk edges, making it the scaffold on which the interferon branch of the KG is built.
authors: Ivashkiv LB, Donlin LT.

title: Interferon-stimulated genes: a complex web of host defenses
why: Catalogues the ISG effector repertoire downstream of ISGF3 with their molecular targets, which is what turns the interferon sub-graph's terminal transcription node into concrete effector->phenotype edges.
authors: Schneider WM, Chevillotte MD, Rice CM.

title: Shared principles in NF-kappaB signaling
why: Single best schema template for the receptor->IKK->IkB->NF-kB backbone, defining the canonical/non-canonical module split and the Rel/IkB node inventory in one authoritative text.
authors: Hayden MS, Ghosh S.

title: The non-canonical NF-κB pathway in immunity and inflammation
why: Supplies the entire non-canonical sub-graph — NIK stabilization, IKKalpha-driven p100->p52 processing, RelB:p52 targets and which TNFSF receptors route there — which the canonical-centric sources omit.
authors: Sun SC.

title: Activation of the IkappaB kinase complex by TRAF6 requires a dimeric ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme complex and a unique polyubiquitin chain
why: Founding evidence that K63 polyubiquitin is a non-degradative activating signal, which is what forces the KG to type ubiquitination edges by linkage rather than as generic 'ubiquitinates' along the IL-1R/TRAF6->IKK path.
authors: Deng L, Wang C, Spencer E, Yang L, Braun A, You J, Slaughter C, Pickart C, Chen ZJ.

title: Induction of TNF receptor I-mediated apoptosis via two sequential signaling complexes
why: Establishes the complex I (membrane, NF-kB-activating) vs complex II (cytosolic, death-inducing) split, giving TNFR1 edges a required compartment attribute and the survival/apoptosis phenotype fork.
authors: Micheau O, Tschopp J.

title: De-ubiquitination and ubiquitin ligase domains of A20 downregulate NF-kappaB signalling
why: Defines the canonical slow negative-feedback node with a two-activity (DUB then E3) edge on RIP1 chains — the ubiquitin-editing mechanism that must be represented for IKK-level feedback to be modelled.
authors: Wertz IE, O'Rourke KM, Zhou H, Eby M, Aravind L, Seshagiri S, Wu P, Wiesmann C, Baker R, Boone DL, Ma A, Koonin EV, Dixit VM.

title: The IkappaB-NF-kappaB signaling module: temporal control and selective gene activation
why: Origin of the temporal-dynamics layer: shows the three IkB isoform feedbacks are non-redundant and generate distinct activity waveforms that select target genes, and supplies the ODE module the field still builds on.
authors: Hoffmann A, Levchenko A, Scott ML, Baltimore D.

title: Oscillations in NF-kappaB signaling control the dynamics of gene expression
why: First live-cell imaging proof of nucleocytoplasmic RelA oscillations whose frequency tunes transcription — the reference that makes 'oscillation period' a legitimate KG attribute rather than an artifact.
authors: Nelson DE, Ihekwaba AE, Elliott M, Johnson JR, Gibney CA, Foreman BE, Nelson G, See V, Horton CA, Spiller DG, Edwards SW, McDowell HP, Unitt JF, Sullivan E, Grimley R, Benson N, Broomhead D, Kell DB, White MR.

title: Single-cell NF-kappaB dynamics reveal digital activation and analogue information processing
why: Microfluidic single-cell measurement showing TNF dose is encoded digitally (fraction of responders) plus analogue (dynamics), which forces the KG to carry per-cell heterogeneity instead of a population-average activity node.
authors: Tay S, Hughey JJ, Lee TK, Lipniacki T, Quake SR, Covert MW.

title: TGF-β signaling in health and disease
why: Single most current authoritative synthesis of the whole cascade — use it as the master node/edge inventory (ligand activation, receptor pairs, R-SMAD/co-SMAD complexes, target programs) that every other entry annotates.
authors: Massagué J, Sheppard D.

title: TGF-β Signaling from Receptors to Smads
journal: Cold Spring Harbor perspectives in biology
why: The step-by-step mechanistic spine of this exact domain — GS-domain transphosphorylation, C-terminal SSXS R-SMAD phosphorylation, SMAD4 complex formation and nuclear translocation — giving the ordered edge sequence the KG chain needs.
authors: Hata A, Chen YG.

title: Specificity, versatility, and control of TGF-β family signaling
why: Supplies the ligand→type II/type I receptor→SMAD2/3-vs-SMAD1/5/8 routing table across ~33 ligands, which is the combinatorial mapping needed to keep the TGF-beta and BMP branches correctly separated in the graph.
authors: Derynck R, Budi EH.

title: Mechanism of activation of the TGF-beta receptor
why: Founding primary evidence for the sequential receptor model (TGFBR2 binds ligand, recruits and transphosphorylates TGFBR1), the root edge from which every downstream SMAD edge in this KG hangs.
authors: Wrana JL, Attisano L, Wieser R, Ventura F, Massagué J.

title: MADR2 is a substrate of the TGFbeta receptor and its phosphorylation is required for nuclear accumulation and signaling
why: Landmark that made SMAD2 a direct receptor-kinase substrate and tied that phosphorylation causally to nuclear accumulation — the primary source for the kinase→substrate→localization edge triple.
authors: Macías-Silva M, Abdollah S, Hoodless PA, Pirone R, Attisano L, Wrana JL.

title: Direct binding of Smad3 and Smad4 to critical TGF beta-inducible elements in the promoter of human plasminogen activator inhibitor-type 1 gene
why: Defines the CAGA-box SMAD-binding element in SERPINE1, the prototypical SMAD→target-gene edge and the basis of the CAGA-luciferase reporter still used as the standard pathway-activity readout.
authors: Dennler S, Itoh S, Vivien D, ten Dijke P, Huet S, Gauthier JM.

title: Identification of Smad7, a TGFbeta-inducible antagonist of TGF-beta signalling
why: Establishes the ligand-induced I-SMAD that blocks receptor-mediated R-SMAD phosphorylation, providing the one negative-feedback edge without which the KG is a purely feed-forward line.
authors: Nakao A, Afrakhte M, Morén A, Nakayama T, Christian JL, Heuchel R, Itoh S, Kawabata M, Heldin NE, Heldin CH, ten Dijke P.

title: A human Mad protein acting as a BMP-regulated transcriptional activator
why: Primary establishment of SMAD1 as the BMP-responsive effector, anchoring the BMP arm of the graph as a distinct receptor→R-SMAD→transcription branch rather than a variant of the TGF-beta arm.
authors: Liu F, Hata A, Baker JC, Doody J, Cárcamo J, Harland RM, Massagué J.

title: Wnt/beta-catenin signaling: components, mechanisms, and diseases
why: Single most systematic component-by-component inventory of the Wnt chain (WNT->FZD/LRP5-6->DVL->APC/Axin/GSK3/CK1 destruction complex->beta-catenin/TCF), which is directly transcribable as the Wnt branch's node/edge list.
authors: MacDonald BT, Tamai K, He X.

title: Wnt/β-Catenin Signaling, Disease, and Emerging Therapeutic Modalities
why: Covers the post-2009 layer the older Wnt map lacks — PORCN/WLS ligand biogenesis, R-spondin/RNF43-ZNRF3 receptor turnover, and stem-cell phenotypic outputs — so the Wnt branch is not frozen at 2009 mechanism.
authors: Nusse R, Clevers H.

title: Role of YAP/TAZ in mechanotransduction
why: Establishes ECM stiffness and cell geometry as first-class upstream stimuli acting on YAP/TAZ largely outside the LATS cascade, forcing the KG to carry mechanical inputs as real edges rather than annotation.
authors: Dupont S, Morsut L, Aragona M, Enzo E, Giulitti S, Cordenonsi M, Zanconato F, Le Digabel J, Forcato M, Bicciato S, Elvassore N, Piccolo S.

title: Mechanisms of Hippo pathway regulation
why: Open-access, mechanism-complete edge list for MST1/2-MAP4K-SAV1-MOB1-LATS1/2-YAP/TAZ including the S127/14-3-3 retention step, making the separate founding primaries redundant for ingestion purposes.
authors: Meng Z, Moroishi T, Guan KL.

title: Genome-wide association between YAP/TAZ/TEAD and AP-1 at enhancers drives oncogenic growth
why: The only genome-wide definition here of the terminal effector->target-gene layer, and it shows the output edge is conditional on AP-1 co-occupancy rather than TEAD alone.
authors: Zanconato F, Forcato M, Battilana G, Azzolin L, Quaranta E, Bodega B, Rosato A, Bicciato S, Cordenonsi M, Piccolo S.

title: The canonical Notch signaling pathway: unfolding the activation mechanism
why: Carries the entire Notch chain in one authoritative reference — ligand-pull, S2/S3 proteolysis, NICD translocation and the RBPJ corepressor-to-coactivator switch — covering receptor, localization and transcriptional layers at once.
authors: Kopan R, Ilagan MX.

title: Hedgehog signalling in the mouse requires intraflagellar transport proteins
why: The genetic discovery that vertebrate Hh transduction requires the primary cilium — the founding evidence that a compartment, not just a protein set, gates the pathway, which is what a localization filter must encode.
authors: Huangfu D, Liu A, Rakeman AS, Murcia NS, Niswander L, Anderson KV.

title: Biochemical mechanisms of vertebrate hedgehog signaling
why: Most rigorous modern account of the Hh chain as actual biochemistry — PTCH1 sterol transport, cholesterol-dependent SMO activation, GPR161/PKA and GLI activator/repressor processing in ciliary compartments — giving each Hh edge a defined mechanism.
authors: Kong JH, Siebold C, Rohatgi R.

title: The protein kinase complement of the human genome
why: Supplies the canonical 518-kinase node list and group/family/subfamily hierarchy that every kinase entity in the KG must be keyed to.
authors: Manning G, Whyte DB, Martinez R, Hunter T, Sudarsanam S.

title: The conformational plasticity of protein kinases
why: Huse & Kuriyan's activation-loop/alphaC framework is the reference model for typing kinase nodes as inactive/primed/active and for the state-transition edges between them.
authors: Huse M, Kuriyan J.

title: Protein kinases: evolution of dynamic regulatory proteins
why: Single best synthesis of the regulatory/catalytic spine architecture (subsuming the two PNAS spine primaries), giving residue-level allostery features usable as kinase-node annotations.
authors: Taylor SS, Kornev AP.

title: Mechanisms of specificity in protein phosphorylation
why: Separates intrinsic consensus-motif specificity from docking, scaffolding and co-localization — the conceptual basis for typing and confidence-weighting kinase->substrate edges rather than treating motif matches as edges.
authors: Ubersax JA, Ferrell JE.

title: An atlas of substrate specificities for the human serine/threonine kinome
why: Directly ingestible PSSMs for 303 Ser/Thr kinases that let the KG score every phosphosite against the whole Ser/Thr kinome instead of relying on curated pairs.
authors: Johnson JL, Yaron TM, Huntsman EM, Kerelsky A, Song J, Regev A, Lin TY, Liberatore K, Cizin DM, Cohen BM, Vasan N, Ma Y, Krismer K, Robles JT, van de Kooij B, van Vlimmeren AE, Andrée-Busch N, Käufer NF, Dorovkov MV, Ryazanov AG, Takagi Y, Kastenhuber ER, Goncalves MD, Hopkins BD, Elemento O, Taatjes DJ, Maucuer A, Yamashita A, Degterev A, Uduman M, Lu J, Landry SD, Zhang B, Cossentino I, Linding R, Blenis J, Hornbeck PV, Turk BE, Yaffe MB, Cantley LC.

title: The intrinsic substrate specificity of the human tyrosine kinome
why: Completes the motif-scoring layer for the pTyr arm (78 tyrosine kinases plus pTyr-reader/phosphatase specificities), enabling receptor-kinase output edges to be scored on the same footing as Ser/Thr.

title: Increased insulin sensitivity and obesity resistance in mice lacking the protein tyrosine phosphatase-1B gene
why: The genetic proof that PTP1B terminates insulin-receptor autophosphorylation in vivo, giving the KG a fully specified receptor→phosphatase→organismal-phenotype chain.
authors: Elchebly M, Payette P, Michaliszyn E, Cromlish W, Collins S, Loy AL, Normandin D, Cheng A, Himms-Hagen J, Chan CC, Ramachandran C, Gresser MJ, Tremblay ML, Kennedy BP.

title: Assembly of cell regulatory systems through protein interaction domains
why: Pawson & Nash's synthesis is the single best statement of the domain-motif grammar the KG's edge schema encodes (modular readers, combinatorial recruitment, allosteric autoinhibition), and it subsumes the 1995 founding essay and the 1997 scaffold/adaptor typology.
authors: Pawson T, Nash P.

title: SH2 domains recognize specific phosphopeptide sequences
why: The degenerate-peptide-library study that produced the first per-SH2 pY+1/+3 selection matrices — still the template for scoring pTyr-site-to-reader edges, and it makes the four downstream SH2 array/inventory papers redundant.

title: The structural basis for 14-3-3:phosphopeptide binding specificity
why: Defines the mode-1 RSXpSXP / mode-2 consensus with structures, giving a directly executable scan rule for annotating 14-3-3 edges on any pSer/pThr site layer — more KG-usable than the 1996 discovery paper or the later site catalogues.
authors: Yaffe MB, Rittinger K, Volinia S, Caron PR, Aitken A, Leffers H, Gamblin SJ, Smerdon SJ, Cantley LC.

title: A specificity map for the PDZ domain family
why: Phage-display specificity classes across the human and worm PDZ families are an ingestible motif-class table for C-terminal PDZ-binding-motif edges, covering the PDZ layer better than the synaptic review or the mouse-proteome affinity survey.
authors: Tonikian R, Zhang Y, Sazinsky SL, Currell B, Yeh JH, Reva B, Held HA, Appleton BA, Evangelista M, Wu Y, Xin X, Chan AC, Seshagiri S, Lasky LA, Sander C, Boone C, Bader GD, Sidhu SS.

title: Phase transitions in the assembly of multivalent signalling proteins
why: Nephrin/NCK/N-WASP reconstitution shows domain-motif valency, not pairwise affinity, sets the assembly threshold — the basis for a mesoscale condensate state layer above binary edges (and the better representative than the 2016 LAT/TCR follow-up).
authors: Li P, Banjade S, Cheng HC, Kim S, Chen B, Guo L, Llaguno M, Hollingsworth JV, King DS, Banani SF, Russo PS, Jiang QX, Nixon BT, Rosen MK.

title: The biochemical basis of an all-or-none cell fate switch in Xenopus oocytes
why: Canonical demonstration that ultrasensitivity plus positive feedback makes MAPK activation bistable per cell while looking graded in bulk — the rule that keeps the KG's evidence layer from conflating population-average and single-cell edges.
authors: Ferrell JE, Machleder EM.

title: p53 dynamics control cell fate
why: Causal proof — pharmacologically converting pulsed p53 into a sustained signal flips arrest to senescence — that the KG must store the dynamic waveform on an edge, not merely node activation state.
authors: Purvis JE, Karhohs KW, Mock C, Batchelor E, Loewer A, Lahav G.

title: Defining network topologies that can achieve biochemical adaptation
why: Exhaustive three-node topology search establishing that only negative-feedback-with-buffer and incoherent-feedforward classes adapt, letting the KG infer dynamic function directly from a subgraph's wiring pattern.
authors: Ma W, Trusina A, El-Samad H, Lim WA, Tang C.

title: Encoding and decoding cellular information through signaling dynamics
why: The schema document for this KG layer: separates amplitude, duration, frequency, delay and rate into distinct channels with named decoder modules, supplying the controlled vocabulary for dynamics attributes.
authors: Purvis JE, Lahav G.

title: Information transduction capacity of noisy biochemical signaling networks
why: Introduces mutual information as a measurable weight on a signaling edge (~1 bit for a single-cell snapshot readout), giving the KG a principled capacity metric and the noise caveat behind temporal/collective averaging.
authors: Cheong R, Rhee A, Wang CJ, Nemenman I, Levchenko A.

title: Transport into and out of the nucleus
journal: Microbiology and molecular biology reviews : MMBR
why: Single source for the controlled vocabulary the localization layer needs (NLS, NES, importin/exportin, Ran-GTP gradient, NPC), so every shuttling edge in the KG can be typed by transport receptor and direction rather than left as free-text 'goes to nucleus'.
authors: Macara IG.

title: The MAPK cascades: signaling components, nuclear roles and mechanisms of nuclear translocation
why: Enumerates, cascade by cascade (ERK/JNK/p38/ERK5), the import mechanism, the retention anchor and the nuclear substrate set — i.e. it can be read off almost directly as kinase→compartment→substrate triples, which is why it beats the individual ERK-translocation primaries for KG construction.
authors: Plotnikov A, Zehorai E, Procaccia S, Seger R.

title: Endocytosis and signalling: intertwining molecular networks
why: The anchor review for treating endosomes/trafficking as signaling nodes rather than degradation sinks — supplies the compartment inventory and adaptor/scaffold vocabulary for every endosomal edge in the KG.
authors: Sorkin A, von Zastrow M.

title: Conformational biosensors reveal GPCR signalling from endosomes
why: The landmark that forced 'where' onto receptor-transducer edges by showing internalized β2AR keeps activating Gs on endosomes; also introduces the nanobody conformational biosensors used to assay compartment-resolved receptor state, so it serves both the localization and evidence layers.
authors: Irannejad R, Tomshine JC, Tomshine JR, Chevalier M, Mahoney JP, Steyaert J, Rasmussen SG, Sunahara RK, El-Samad H, Huang B, von Zastrow M.

title: The mystery of membrane organization: composition, regulation and roles of lipid rafts
why: Supersedes the 2000 raft manifesto with the nanoscale, dynamic picture, so membrane-microdomain annotations in the KG encode transient nanodomains with defined lipid/protein determinants instead of the discredited static-raft ontology.
authors: Sezgin E, Levental I, Mayor S, Eggeling C.

title: High-sensitivity measurements of multiple kinase activities in live single cells
why: Kinase translocation reporters turned kinase activity into a readable nucleocytoplasmic ratio and are the source of most single-cell spatial-signaling data the KG will ingest, so this is the method paper the evidence layer must cite for that assay class.
authors: Regot S, Hughey JJ, Bajar BT, Carrasco S, Covert MW.

title: Calcium signaling
why: Single best entry point for the Ca2+ layer: enumerates channels, pumps, buffers and sensors as discrete node types and states the microdomain/spatial rules that every downstream Ca2+ edge must be annotated with.
authors: Clapham DE.

title: Store-Operated Calcium Channels
why: Gives the complete store-depletion -> STIM1 -> Orai1 CRAC chain with ER-PM junction geometry and the human ORAI1/STIM1 loss-of-function genetics, so one source instantiates the whole SOCE branch including its immune phenotypes.
authors: Prakriya M, Lewis RS.

title: Mechanisms of CaMKII action in long-term potentiation
why: Supplies the concrete Ca2+/CaM -> CaMKII autophosphorylation -> substrate (GluN2B, AMPAR, actin regulators) edge set plus the translocation step, which is what makes CaMKII representable as localized kinase-substrate relations rather than a generic hub.
authors: Lisman J, Yasuda R, Raghavachari S.

title: Transcriptional regulation by calcium, calcineurin, and NFAT
why: The canonical statement of the only Ca2+/CaM-activated phosphatase arm, giving a fully specified Ca2+ -> CaM -> calcineurin -> NFAT dephosphorylation -> nuclear import -> transcription chain that closes the loop from second messenger to cell state.
authors: Hogan PG, Chen L, Nardone J, Rao A.

title: AKAP signalling complexes: focal points in space and time
why: Defines the scaffold as a first-class node type - AKAPs co-recruiting PKA with its substrates, PDEs and phosphatases - which is the ontological primitive the KG needs to encode why a kinase acts on one substrate and not another.
authors: Wong W, Scott JD.

title: Phosphoinositides: tiny lipids with giant impact on cell regulation
why: The most complete enzyme-by-enzyme inventory of PI kinases, phosphatases, PLC isozymes and effector-domain readers, effectively a ready-made edge list for the entire lipid second-messenger layer.
authors: Balla T.

title: Phosphoinositides as membrane organizers
why: Current authority on PI-defined organelle identity, effector recruitment and lipid transfer at contact sites - the localization vocabulary that turns lipid nodes into compartment-tagged entities and updates the pre-2015 PI reviews.
authors: Posor Y, Jang W, Haucke V.

title: The ubiquitin code
why: Defines the writer/reader/eraser + linkage-type schema that the ubiquitin edge model of the KG should literally be built on.
authors: Komander D, Rape M.

title: An expanded lexicon for the ubiquitin code
why: Extends the edge vocabulary to branched/hybrid chains, M1, and non-lysine (Ser/Thr/Cys) conjugation so modification-state nodes are not artificially restricted to K48/K63.
authors: Dikic I, Schulman BA.

title: Structural insights into the catalysis and regulation of E3 ubiquitin ligases
why: Single best mechanistic taxonomy of RING/HECT/RBR E3s and their activation switches — supplies the enzyme-class and regulation attributes for every E3 node (supersedes the 'at a glance' and CRL-only entries).
authors: Buetow L, Huang DT.

title: Mechanisms of Deubiquitinase Specificity and Regulation
why: Gives the DUB family set plus linkage- and substrate-specificity rules needed to type erase-edges by chain linkage rather than as a generic 'removes ubiquitin' relation.
authors: Mevissen TET, Komander D.

title: The Logic of the 26S Proteasome
why: Specifies how the proteasome recognises, deubiquitinates and unfolds substrates, i.e. the decision rules for when a K48-type edge actually terminates a signaling node.
authors: Collins GA, Goldberg AL.

title: The ubiquitin kinase PINK1 recruits autophagy receptors to induce mitophagy
why: Encodes a complete phospho-ubiquitin crosstalk chain (kinase writes on ubiquitin -> reader recruitment -> organelle phenotype), the cleanest template for conditional two-PTM edges with a localization filter.
authors: Lazarou M, Sliter DA, Kane LA, Sarraf SA, Wang C, Burman JL, Sideris DP, Fogel AI, Youle RJ.

title: Ubiquitin ligase activity and tyrosine phosphorylation underlie suppression of growth factor signaling by c-Cbl/Sli-1
why: Archetype of the opposite crosstalk direction — receptor phosphotyrosine recruits an E3 that terminates RTK signaling — anchoring the growth-factor arm that the NF-kB/mitophagy papers do not cover.
authors: Levkowitz G, Waterman H, Ettenberg SA, Katz M, Tsygankov AY, Alroy I, Lavi S, Iwai K, Reiss Y, Ciechanover A, Lipkowitz S, Yarden Y.

title: Systematic and quantitative assessment of the ubiquitin-modified proteome
why: The diGly-proteomics reference dataset: thousands of site-level ubiquitination calls with proteasome-dependence, directly ingestible as substrate/site nodes with measurement evidence.
authors: Kim W, Bennett EJ, Huttlin EL, Guo A, Li J, Possemato A, Sowa ME, Rad R, Rush J, Comb MJ, Harper JW, Gygi SP.

title: Molecular mechanisms of cell death: recommendations of the Nomenclature Committee on Cell Death 2018
why: Supplies the consensus controlled vocabulary (apoptosis vs pyroptosis vs necroptosis vs ferroptosis, each with molecular criteria) that the KG's phenotype nodes must be typed against, so effector-to-outcome edges resolve to defined death modalities rather than free text.

title: Regulation of apoptosis in health and disease: the balancing act of BCL-2 family proteins
why: The single best modern statement of BCL-2 family interaction rules (pro-survival sequestration, BH3-only activators vs sensitizers, BAX/BAK oligomerisation), which is exactly the typed edge grammar needed for the intrinsic-apoptosis effector subgraph.

title: Proapoptotic BAX and BAK: a requisite gateway to mitochondrial dysfunction and death
why: Double-knockout genetics proving BAX/BAK are the obligate convergence node for essentially all intrinsic death stimuli — the one apoptosis edge the KG can encode as a hard bottleneck rather than a modulatory influence.
authors: Wei MC, Zong WX, Cheng EH, Lindsten T, Panoutsakopoulou V, Ross AJ, Roth KA, MacGregor GR, Thompson CB, Korsmeyer SJ.

title: Caspases in Cell Death, Inflammation, and Disease
why: Maps every apoptotic and inflammatory caspase to its activating platform (apoptosome, DISC, inflammasome) and its downstream substrate/phenotype, giving the caspase half of the effector layer in one authoritative pass and replacing the several narrower caspase papers in the candidate set.
authors: Van Opdenbosch N, Lamkanfi M.

title: The proliferation-quiescence decision is controlled by a bifurcation in CDK2 activity at mitotic exit
why: Live-cell CDK2 biosensor work showing a continuous kinase activity variable bifurcates sister cells into discrete proliferative vs quiescent states — the template for representing cell-cycle cell-state nodes as quantitative kinase-activity variables rather than static labels.
authors: Spencer SL, Cappell SD, Tsai FC, Overton KW, Wang CL, Meyer T.

title: Control of cell cycle transcription during G1 and S phases
why: Lays out the CDK-to-RB-to-E2F-to-gene-module chain with its feedback loops, providing the kinase-phosphorylates-substrate plus TF-activates-program edges that connect cell-cycle kinases to their transcriptional output.
authors: Bertoli C, Skotheim JM, de Bruin RA.

title: Putting p53 in Context
why: The definitive argument that one phospho-regulated TF routes to arrest, apoptosis or senescence depending on cell context — the reference justifying context-conditioned effector-to-phenotype edges instead of a single fixed p53 output, and the natural hinge between the apoptosis and cell-cycle subgraphs.
authors: Kastenhuber ER, Lowe SW.

title: The integrated stress response: From mechanism to disease
why: Current mechanistic account of the four eIF2alpha kinases converging on eIF2/eIF2B and the ATF4 output, plus ISRIB as a defined node perturbation — a clean multi-input/single-effector translation module that supersedes the 2016 EMBO Reports ISR review in the same list.
authors: Costa-Mattioli M, Walter P.

title: Regulation and metabolic functions of mTORC1 and mTORC2
why: Comprehensive substrate and lysosomal-localization map for the mTOR complexes, defining the growth-signal hub whose 4E-BP1/S6K/ULK1 edges feed the translation-control and cell-cycle effector layers.
authors: Szwed A, Kim E, Jacinto E.

title: T cell activation
why: Single most complete backbone edge list for the TCR arm (ITAM->LCK->ZAP70->LAT/SLP-76->PLCg1/Ras/PKC), and it subsumes the three narrower TCR-initiation reviews in the candidate pool.
authors: Smith-Garvin JE, Koretzky GA, Jordan MS.

title: Phase separation of signaling molecules promotes T cell receptor signal transduction
why: Reconstitution landmark that forces the KG to model LAT/Grb2/SOS1 condensates as a compartment node gating propagation, rather than treating LAT phosphorylation as a plain kinase-substrate edge.
authors: Su X, Ditlev JA, Hui E, Xing W, Banjade S, Okrut J, King DS, Taunton J, Rosen MK, Vale RD.

title: Systems-level conservation of the proximal TCR signaling network of mice and humans
why: The only directly ingestible edge set in the pool: AP-MS interactomes for 20+ proximal TCR baits in primary mouse and human T cells, with species annotation and per-edge evidence weights.
authors: Nicolas P, Ollier J, Mori D, Voisinne G, Celis-Gutierrez J, Gregoire C, Perroteau J, Vivien R, Camus M, Burlet-Schiltz O, Gonzalez de Peredo A, Clémenceau B, Roncagalli R, Vié H, Malissen B.

title: The SYK tyrosine kinase: a crucial  player in diverse biological functions
why: Best single source for the BCR/ITAM arm and the one that makes SYK a shared hub node across BCR, FcR and integrin inputs — covers the BTK/BLNK/PLCg2 chain that the narrower DT40 and BTK papers only supply piecewise.
authors: Mócsai A, Ruland J, Tybulewicz VL.

title: Toll-like Receptors and the Control of Immunity
why: Schema reference for the whole TLR arm: ligand->receptor->MyD88/TRIF adaptor branching plus the compartment-conditioned outputs, making the separate TRAM, CD14 and TLR4-MD2 primaries redundant here.
authors: Fitzgerald KA, Kagan JC.

title: Helical assembly in the MyD88-IRAK4-IRAK2 complex in TLR/IL-1R signalling
why: Myddosome structure converts the MyD88->IRAK4->IRAK2 adaptor arrow into a stoichiometric, ordered complex node — the structural grounding the IRAK4 discovery paper cannot provide.
authors: Lin SC, Lo YC, Wu H.

title: The NLRP3 inflammasome: molecular activation and regulation to therapeutics
why: Supplies the two-signal priming-then-triggering pattern that the KG needs as a general licensing-edge template, and carries the caspase-1/GSDMD/IL-1b output chain for the inflammasome arm.
authors: Swanson KV, Deng M, Ting JP.

title: T cell costimulatory receptor CD28 is a primary target for PD-1-mediated inhibition
why: Pins the checkpoint arm to a precise PD-1/SHP2->CD28 dephosphorylation edge instead of a vague inhibitory arrow, and anchors both the costimulation and checkpoint node sets in one reconstituted mechanism.
authors: Hui E, Cheung J, Zhu J, Su X, Taylor MJ, Wallweber HA, Sasmal DK, Huang J, Kim JM, Mellman I, Vale RD.

title: Principles of interleukin (IL)-6-type cytokine signalling and its regulation
why: The single most complete edge-level account of gp130 complex stoichiometry -> JAK1/JAK2/TYK2 -> STAT1/3 and SHP2-ERK branching plus SOCS/PTP feedback, giving both activating and inhibitory edges for the entire IL-6-family arm.
authors: Heinrich PC, Behrmann I, Haan S, Hermanns HM, Müller-Newen G, Schaper F.

title: The JAK-STAT pathway at twenty
why: Supplies the canonical receptor-chain -> JAK -> STAT pairing inventory (4 JAKs, 7 STATs) that a KG needs to disambiguate which cytokine routes to which transcription factor, rather than collapsing all cytokines into one generic cascade.
authors: Stark GR, Darnell JE.

title: The IL-23-IL-17 immune axis: from mechanisms to therapeutic testing
why: Definitive wiring of IL-23 -> Th17/ILC3 cell-state transition -> IL-17 effector output, the reference template for cytokine->cell-state->cytokine relay edges that pure receptor-cascade sources cannot express.
authors: Gaffen SL, Jain R, Garg AV, Cua DJ.

title: IL-17 receptor-based signaling and implications for disease
why: Encodes the non-JAK cytokine cascade the KG would otherwise miss: SEFIR/Act1 -> TRAF6 -> NF-kB versus TRAF2/5 -> mRNA-stabilization, adding a post-transcriptional effector node type.
authors: Li X, Bechara R, Zhao J, McGeachy MJ, Gaffen SL.

title: The TNF and TNF receptor superfamilies: integrating mammalian biology
why: The complete TNFSF/TNFRSF ligand-receptor pairing roster, directly ingestible as the node and binding-edge table for the whole TNF superfamily including death-domain vs TRAF-binding receptor classes.
authors: Locksley RM, Killeen N, Lenardo MJ.

title: TNF-R1 signaling: a beautiful pathway
why: Canonical, compact map of TRADD/TRAF2/RIP -> IKK/NF-kB versus FADD/caspase-8 from one receptor, the reference case for encoding mutually exclusive downstream phenotypes off a single node.
authors: Chen G, Goeddel DV.

title: A guide to chemokines and their receptors
why: Open-access tabulation of every human chemokine, conventional receptor and atypical/scavenging receptor with signaling outputs — the one candidate that can be ingested wholesale as the chemokine node/edge table, superseding the older nomenclature and narrative reviews.
authors: Hughes CE, Nibbs RJB.

title: Getting to the site of inflammation: the leukocyte adhesion cascade updated
why: Defines the ordered capture -> rolling -> chemokine-triggered integrin activation -> arrest -> transmigration chain, the downstream phenotype sequence every chemokine-receptor edge in the KG ultimately terminates in.
authors: Ley K, Laudanna C, Cybulsky MI, Nourshargh S.

title: Network motifs: theory and experimental approaches
why: Single best source for mapping each recurring subgraph type (coherent/incoherent FFL, SIM, DOR, feedback) to a concrete dynamic function, so motif annotations on KG subgraphs carry predicted behaviour rather than just topology.
authors: Alon U.

title: Robustness in simple biochemical networks
why: Origin of the claim that exact adaptation is a structural, parameter-independent property, which justifies treating KG topology (not rate constants) as the object that predicts robust signaling behaviour.
authors: Barkai N, Leibler S.

title: Emergent properties of networks of biological signaling pathways
why: The founding demonstration that bistability and memory arise only from interconnecting pathways, which is the core justification for storing signaling as a crosstalk-bearing graph instead of independent linear cascades.
authors: Bhalla US, Iyengar R.

title: Combinatorial Signal Perception in the BMP Pathway
why: Shows promiscuous ligand-receptor pairing computes ligand combinations rather than summing single inputs, directly invalidating one-ligand-one-edge encoding and motivating receptor-repertoire-conditioned edges.
authors: Antebi YE, Linton JM, Klumpe H, Bintu B, Gong M, Su C, McCardell R, Elowitz MB.

title: Master transcription factors determine cell-type-specific responses to TGF-β signaling
why: Demonstrates that lineage master TFs redirect the same SMAD effector to different enhancers per cell type, giving the mechanistic rule for conditioning shared-pathway effector edges on cell state.
authors: Mullen AC, Orlando DA, Newman JJ, Lovén J, Kumar RM, Bilodeau S, Reddy J, Guenther MG, DeKoter RP, Young RA.

title: PhosphoSitePlus, 2014: mutations, PTMs and recalibrations
why: Supplies the canonical site nomenclature and the curated kinase-substrate ground-truth set against which every motif-predicted edge in the KG is labelled known vs predicted.
authors: Hornbeck PV, Zhang B, Murray B, Kornhauser JM, Latham V, Skrzypek E.

title: The functional landscape of the human phosphoproteome
why: Supplies a functional-importance score for ~120k human sites, letting the KG down-weight the vast bystander fraction instead of treating every detected phosphosite as a signaling node.
authors: Ochoa D, Jarnuczak AF, Viéitez C, Gehre M, Soucheray M, Mateus A, Kleefeldt AA, Hill A, Garcia-Alonso L, Stein F, Krogan NJ, Savitski MM, Swaney DL, Vizcaíno JA, Noh KM, Beltrao P.

authors: Bunne C, Roohani Y, Rosen Y, Gupta A, Zhang X, Roed M, Alexandrov T, AlQuraishi M, Brennan P, Burkhardt DB, Califano A, Cool J, Dernburg AF, Ewing K, Fox EB, Haury M, Herr AE, Horvitz E, Hsu PD, Jain V, Johnson GR, Kalil T, Kelley DR, Kelley SO, Kreshuk A, Mitchison T, Otte S, Shendure J, Sofroniew NJ, Theis F, Theodoris CV, Upadhyayula S, Valer M, Wang B, Xing E, Yeung-Levy S, Zitnik M, Karaletsos T, Regev A, Lundberg E, Leskovec J, Quake SR.

title: scGPT: toward building a foundation model for single-cell multi-omics using generative AI

title: Integrated intra- and intercellular signaling knowledge for multicellular omics analysis

authors: Türei D, Valdeolivas A, Gul L, Palacio-Escat N, Klein M, Ivanova O, Ölbei M, Gábor A, Theis F, Módos D, Korcsmáros T, Saez-Rodriguez J.

title: CRISPR activation and interference screens decode stimulation responses in primary human T cells

title: AMPK: guardian of metabolism and mitochondrial homeostasis

title: AMPK: a nutrient and energy sensor that maintains energy homeostasis
why: Complementary canonical AMPK mechanism review detailing LKB1/CaMKK2 upstream inputs and ACC/mTOR/ULK1 substrates for the kinase-cascade layer.
authors: Hardie DG, Ross FA, Hawley SA.

title: Rho GTPases: biochemistry and biology
journal: Annual review of cell and developmental biology
why: Supplies the missing RhoA/Rac1/Cdc42 master-switch node upstream of the KG's cytoskeletal actin effectors driving morphology and migration phenotypes.
authors: Jaffe AB, Hall A.

title: The integrin adhesome: from genes and proteins to human disease
why: Introduces integrins as a major non-RTK receptor class and inventories the focal-adhesion effectors (FAK/paxillin/talin/vinculin) already present in the KG.
authors: Winograd-Katz SE, Fässler R, Geiger B, Legate KR.

title: Molecular mechanisms of necroptosis: an ordered cellular explosion
why: Adds the RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL necroptotic death branch missing from the apoptosis-only survival_death effector layer.
authors: Vandenabeele P, Galluzzi L, Vanden Berghe T, Kroemer G.

title: The gasdermins, a protein family executing cell death and inflammation
why: Covers the GSDMD pore-forming executioner linking the KG's existing NLRP3 inflammasome to lytic pyroptotic death and IL-1 release.
authors: Broz P, Pelegrín P, Shao F.

title: Ferroptosis: A Regulated Cell Death Nexus Linking Metabolism, Redox Biology, and Disease
why: Definitive review of the GPX4/iron/lipid-peroxidation death program, a metabolism-coupled modality with zero representation in survival_death.
authors: Stockwell BR, Friedmann Angeli JP, Bayir H, Bush AI, Conrad M, Dixon SJ, Fulda S, Gascón S, Hatzios SK, Kagan VE, Noel K, Jiang X, Linkermann A, Murphy ME, Overholtzer M, Oyagi A, Pagnussat GC, Park J, Ran Q, Rosenfeld CS, Salnikow K, Tang D, Torti FM, Torti SV, Toyokuni S, Woerpel KA, Zhang DD.

title: Autophagy fights disease through cellular self-digestion
why: Foundational autophagy review anchoring the mTOR/AMPK-to-ULK1/BECN1 machinery the KG already enumerates in vesicle_trafficking.
authors: Mizushima N, Levine B, Cuervo AM, Klionsky DJ.

title: Trained immunity: A program of innate immune memory in health and disease
why: Founding reference for the innate-memory concept on which immune-circuits.md builds its Trained Immunity and inflammaging circuits.
authors: Netea MG, Joosten LA, Latz E, Mills KH, Natoli G, Stunnenberg HG, O'Neill LA, Xavier RJ.

title: Defining trained immunity and its role in health and disease
why: Mechanistic definitional update (epigenetic plus metabolic reprogramming) that operationalizes the trained-immunity lock-in circuit.
authors: Netea MG, Domínguez-Andrés J, Barreiro LB, Chavakis T, Divangahi M, Fuchs E, Joosten LAB, van der Meer JWM, Mhlanga MM, Mulder WJM, Riksen NP, Schlitzer A, Schultze JL, Stabell Benn C, Sun JC, Xavier RJ, Latz E.

title: IL-33, an interleukin-1-like cytokine that signals via the IL-1 receptor-related protein ST2
why: Landmark discovery paper defining IL-33/ST2 signaling, the cornerstone of the KG's dedicated alarmin circuit.
authors: Schmitz J, Owyang A, Oldham E, Song Y, Murphy E, McClanahan TK, Zurawski G, Moshrefi M, Qin J, Li X, Gorman DM, Bazan JF, Kastelein RA.

title: Complement System Part I - Molecular Mechanisms of Activation and Regulation
why: Comprehensive open-access review of classical/lectin/alternative complement activation and regulation, filling a total complement blind spot behind Pillar 4.
authors: Merle NS, Church SE, Fremeaux-Bacchi V, Roumenina LT.

title: Fcgamma receptors as regulators of immune responses
why: Canonical review of activating/inhibitory FcgR balance and ADCC underpinning the autoantibody-mediated-disease circuit.
authors: Nimmerjahn F, Ravetch JV.

title: Myeloid-derived suppressor cells as regulators of the immune system
why: Foundational MDSC biology filling the TME MDSC-lock node absent from the KG's TAM/Treg/exhaustion context.
authors: Gabrilovich DI, Nagaraj S.

title: A guide to immunometabolism for immunologists
why: Ties signaling to immune-cell metabolic state (Warburg/lactate/adenosine), connecting the metabolic effector layer to the TME metabolic circuits.
authors: O'Neill LA, Kishton RJ, Rathmell J.

title: The nuclear receptor superfamily: The second decade
why: The field-defining synthesis that formalized the nuclear receptor superfamily's shared domain architecture (DBD/LBD), classified receptor subfamilies (steroid, RXR-heterodimerizing, orphan), and named the mechanism vocabulary the whole sub-topic's node/edge types trace back to.
authors: Mangelsdorf DJ, Thummel C, Beato M, Herrlich P, Schütz G, Umesono K, Blumberg B, Kastner P, Mark M, Chambon P, Evans RM.

title: The steroid and thyroid hormone receptor superfamily
why: The original review proposing that steroid, thyroid hormone, and retinoic acid receptors form one gene superfamily of ligand-activated transcription factors, the founding conceptual edge this domain's KG must anchor on before any specific receptor subtype is added.
authors: Evans RM.

title: The coregulator exchange in transcriptional functions of nuclear receptors
why: Establishes the corepressor-to-coactivator exchange model that is the core mechanistic edge separating genomic nuclear receptor signaling from simple ligand-binding, essential for the coregulator-recruitment node type the domain needs.
authors: Glass CK, Rosenfeld MG.

title: Combinatorial control of gene expression by nuclear receptors and coregulators
why: Reviews how hundreds of coregulator proteins combine with a limited receptor repertoire to give tissue- and gene-specific outputs, supplying the many-to-many coregulator-receptor edge semantics that a KG modeling combinatorial control needs to represent correctly.
authors: McKenna NJ, O'Malley BW.

title: Convergence of 9-cis retinoic acid and peroxisome proliferator signalling pathways through heterodimer formation of their receptors
why: Discovers that RXR heterodimerizes with PPAR to integrate two distinct ligand signals at one response element, the mechanistic origin of the RXR-heterodimer node/edge structure that PPAR, RAR, TR and VDR signaling all depend on.
authors: Kliewer SA, Umesono K, Noonan DJ, Heyman RA, Evans RM.

title: Steroid Receptor Interactions with Heat Shock Protein and Immunophilin Chaperones
why: Defines the cytoplasmic hsp90/hsp70/immunophilin chaperone complex that holds unliganded steroid receptors in a ligand-binding-competent state, the chaperone-complex node needed before receptor activation can be modeled as a multi-step process.
authors: Pratt WB, Toft DO.

title: The RXR heterodimers and orphan receptors
why: Companion piece to the superfamily review, focused on RXR as the shared heterodimerization hub and orphan receptors awaiting ligand assignment, clarifying which nuclear receptor nodes are ligand-dependent vs still-orphan.
authors: Mangelsdorf DJ, Evans RM.

title: An Antidiabetic Thiazolidinedione Is a High Affinity Ligand for Peroxisome Proliferator-activated Receptor gamma (PPARgamma)
why: Identifies thiazolidinedione antidiabetic drugs as direct PPARgamma ligands, linking a nuclear receptor node to both an endogenous-signaling role and a drug-target edge, the concrete ligand-receptor-effector example the domain needs beyond classic steroid/retinoid cases.
authors: Lehmann JM, Moore LB, Smith-Oliver TA, Wilkison WO, Willson TM, Kliewer SA.

title: Sensors and signals: a coactivator/corepressor/epigenetic code for integrating signal-dependent programs of transcriptional response
why: Extends the coregulator-exchange model to show how nuclear receptors integrate signal-dependent cues into transcriptional outcomes via a combinatorial epigenetic code, supplying crosstalk edges linking nuclear receptor signaling to upstream kinase cascades and chromatin state.
authors: Rosenfeld MG, Lunyak VV, Glass CK.

title: Cryo-EM reveals how Hsp90 and FKBP immunophilins co-regulate the glucocorticoid receptor
why: First structural (cryo-EM) view of the intact Hsp90-glucocorticoid receptor-immunophilin maturation complex, giving the chaperone-complex node a concrete recent structural anchor rather than only the 1997 biochemical model, the domain's one clearly 2018-plus mechanistic addition.
authors: Noddings CM, Johnson JL, Agard DA.

title: Cyclic GMP-AMP Synthase Is a Cytosolic DNA Sensor That Activates the Type I Interferon Pathway
why: Discovers cGAS as the cytosolic DNA sensor that synthesizes cGAMP to activate STING, the founding receptor-node/second-messenger-edge of the entire cGAS-STING sensing cascade this sub-topic needs.
authors: Sun L, Wu J, Du F, Chen X, Chen ZJ.

title: STING is an endoplasmic reticulum adaptor that facilitates innate immune signalling
why: Identifies STING as the ER-resident adaptor that transduces cytosolic-DNA-sensing signals to TBK1-IRF3, the adaptor node discovered before cGAS itself, and the direct downstream partner every cGAS-STING mechanistic paper depends on.
authors: Ishikawa H, Barber GN.

title: Structural mechanism of cytosolic DNA sensing by cGAS
why: Solves the cGAS-DNA complex structure, showing dsDNA-length-dependent cGAS oligomerization as the trigger for catalytic activation, giving the receptor_structure layer a concrete ligand-sensing mechanism to complement the Sun 2013 discovery paper.
authors: Civril F, Deimling T, de Oliveira Mann CC, Ablasser A, Moldt M, Witte G, Hornung V, Hopfner KP.

title: Structural basis of STING binding with and phosphorylation by TBK1
why: Structurally resolves the STING-TBK1 complex and how TBK1 phosphorylates STING's pLxIS motif to recruit IRF3, supplying the precise kinase-substrate edge that completes the cGAS-STING cascade this sub-topic anchors.
authors: Zhang C, Shang G, Gui X, Zhang X, Bai XC, Chen ZJ.

title: The Inflammasome: A Molecular Platform Triggering Activation of Inflammatory Caspases and Processing of proIL-beta
why: Coins the term 'inflammasome' and defines the NLR/ASC/caspase-1 multiprotein-complex assembly model that every later NLRP3/AIM2 structural paper builds on, the foundational effector-assembly node the sub-topic's inflammasome branch needs.
authors: Martinon F, Burns K, Tschopp J.

title: Unified Polymerization Mechanism for the Assembly of ASC-Dependent Inflammasomes
why: Shows via cryo-EM that diverse NLR/ALR sensors (NLRP3, AIM2, NLRC4) all nucleate ASC filament polymerization by a shared prion-like mechanism, giving the KG a single unifying assembly-edge type instead of a separate one per sensor family.
authors: Lu A, Magupalli VG, Ruan J, Yin Q, Atianand MK, Vos MR, Schröder GF, Fitzgerald KA, Wu H, Egelman EH.

title: AIM2 recognizes cytosolic dsDNA and forms a caspase-1-activating inflammasome with ASC
why: Identifies AIM2 as a non-NLR (HIN-200 family) cytosolic dsDNA sensor that nucleates an ASC/caspase-1 inflammasome independent of NLRP3, broadening the sensor-node vocabulary beyond TLRs/NLRs to the ALR family.
authors: Hornung V, Ablasser A, Charrel-Dennis M, Bauernfeind F, Horvath G, Caffrey DR, Latz E, Fitzgerald KA.

title: Structural Basis for the Activation of Innate Immune Pattern-Recognition Receptor RIG-I by Viral RNA
why: Resolves the RIG-I-dsRNA complex and shows how blunt-end dsRNA binding triggers the conformational change that exposes the CARD domains for MAVS signaling, anchoring the RIG-I-like-receptor branch with a mechanistic structure rather than only the closed-access 2004 discovery paper.
authors: Kowalinski E, Lunardi T, McCarthy AA, Louber J, Brunel J, Grigorov B, Gerlier D, Cusack S.

title: Nod2, a Nod1/Apaf-1 Family Member That Is Restricted to Monocytes and Activates NF-kappaB
why: Discovers NOD2 as an intracellular NLR that senses bacterial peptidoglycan (muramyl dipeptide) and activates NF-kB, completing the sub-topic's sensor coverage with the NLR/NF-kB-signaling branch, distinct from the NLRP3 inflammasome branch, which the domain otherwise lacked entirely.
authors: Ogura Y, Inohara N, Benito A, Chen FF, Yamaoka S, Nunez G.

title: Wnt/β-catenin signalling: function, biological mechanisms, and therapeutic opportunities
why: Comprehensive up-to-date mechanistic and therapeutic-target overview complementing macdonald2009/nusse2017; anchors current receptor/co-receptor node list and Wnt-targeted-therapy edges not covered by the older reviews already in corpus.
authors: Liu J, Xiao Q, Xiao J, Niu C, Li Y, Zhang X, Zhou Z, Shu G, Yin G.

title: Frizzled and LRP5/6 Receptors for Wnt/β-Catenin Signaling
journal: Cold Spring Harbor Perspectives in Biology
why: Dedicated receptor-complex mechanism paper (Frizzled/LRP5-6 co-receptor assembly, Dishevelled recruitment) anchoring receptor-level KG nodes/edges that the two existing broad pathway reviews only summarize.
authors: MacDonald BT, He X.

title: Axin-mediated CKI phosphorylation of β-catenin at Ser 45: a molecular switch for the Wnt pathway
why: Primary mechanistic paper defining the Axin/CK1/GSK3 destruction-complex phosphorylation switch on beta-catenin; anchors kinase-substrate edges (CK1 to Ser45 priming, GSK3 to downstream sites) absent from the pathway-overview papers already in corpus.
authors: Amit S, Hatzubai A, Birman Y, Andersen JS, Ben-Shushan E, Mann M, Ben-Neriah Y, Alkalay I.

title: Wnt-Frizzled/Planar Cell Polarity Signaling: Cellular Orientation by Facing the Wind (Wnt)
journal: Annual Review of Cell and Developmental Biology
why: Dedicated review of the non-canonical planar-cell-polarity (PCP) branch (Frizzled/Dishevelled/Vangl/core PCP proteins), a distinct signaling output from canonical beta-catenin signaling not covered anywhere in the existing corpus.
authors: Yang Y, Mlodzik M.

title: Wnt signaling in cancer
why: Disease-application review connecting Wnt pathway mutations (APC, CTNNB1, RNF43) to colorectal and other cancers; anchors mutation/disease-association edges not covered by the mechanism-focused Wnt papers above.
authors: Zhan T, Rindtorff N, Boutros M.

title: Notch signaling pathway: architecture, disease, and therapeutics
why: Comprehensive up-to-date architecture and therapeutics review complementing kopan2009; anchors current inhibitor/therapeutic-target edges (gamma-secretase inhibitors, antibody blockers) and full receptor/ligand paralog list not covered by the single existing Notch paper.
authors: Zhou B, Lin W, Long Y, Yang Y, Zhang H, Wu K, Chu Q.

title: Notch-Jagged complex structure implicates a catch bond in tuning ligand sensitivity
why: Structural mechanism paper resolving the Notch1-Jagged1 EGF-domain interface and a force-dependent catch-bond binding mode; anchors specific ligand-receptor structural edges absent from the existing generic pathway review.
authors: Luca VC, Kim BC, Ge C, Kakuda S, Wu D, Roein-Peikar M, Haltiwanger RS, Zhu C, Ha T, Garcia KC.

title: Crystal Structure of the CSL-Notch-Mastermind Ternary Complex Bound to DNA
why: Founding structural paper for the CSL(RBPJ)/Notch-ICD/Mastermind transcriptional activation complex; anchors the specific transcription-factor-assembly edges downstream of Notch cleavage that kopan2009 discusses only narratively.
authors: Wilson JJ, Kovall RA.

title: Metalloprotease ADAM10 Is Required for Notch1 Site 2 Cleavage
why: Direct mechanistic paper establishing ADAM10 (not ADAM17) as the physiological S2 sheddase that primes Notch1 for gamma-secretase cleavage; anchors the specific protease-substrate edge in the proteolytic activation cascade.
authors: van Tetering G, van Diest P, Verlaan I, van der Wall E, Kopan R, Vooijs M.

title: Mutual Inactivation of Notch Receptors and Ligands Facilitates Developmental Patterning
why: Combined experimental/modeling paper establishing cis-inhibition between Notch and Delta within the same cell as the mechanism generating mutually-exclusive sender/receiver states (lateral inhibition); anchors cis- vs trans-interaction edges not present elsewhere in the corpus.
authors: Sprinzak D, Lakhanpal A, LeBon L, Garcia-Ojalvo J, Elowitz MB.

title: Gli Proteins: Regulation in Development and Cancer
why: Dedicated review of GLI1/2/3 transcription-factor processing (activator vs repressor forms), primary-cilium trafficking, and cancer roles; anchors GLI-node regulatory edges that huangfu2003 (cilium transport) and kong2019 (general biochemistry) do not detail.
authors: Niewiadomski P, Niedziółka SM, Markiewicz Ł, Uśpieński T, Baran B, Chojnowska K.

title: Cholesterol activates the G-protein coupled receptor Smoothened to promote Hedgehog signaling
why: Primary mechanistic paper identifying cholesterol binding to Smoothened's extracellular cysteine-rich domain as the endogenous activating ligand; anchors the Patched-to-Smoothened de-repression edge at the molecular-ligand level, a mechanism only alluded to in kong2019.
authors: Luchetti G, Sircar R, Kong JH, Nachtergaele S, Sagner A, Byrne EF, Covey DF, Siebold C, Rohatgi R.

title: Structural basis of Smoothened regulation by its extracellular domains
why: Cryo-EM structure of full-length Smoothened showing how its cysteine-rich and seven-transmembrane domains communicate; anchors a structural node for Smoothened conformational states referenced only abstractly by kong2019.
authors: Byrne EFX, Sircar R, Miller PS, Hedger G, Luchetti G, Nachtergaele S, Tully MD, Mydock-McGrane L, Covey DF, Rambo RP, Sansom MSP, Newstead S, Rohatgi R, Siebold C.

title: Structural basis of sterol recognition by human hedgehog receptor PTCH1
why: Cryo-EM structure of Patched1 (PTCH1) bound to cholesterol/sterol substrates, showing how PTCH1 exports sterols to suppress Smoothened; anchors the specific Patched-sterol-transport edge upstream of the Smoothened activation mechanism above.
authors: Qi C, Di Minin G, Vercellino I, Wutz A, Korkhov VM.

title: The role of the Hedgehog signaling pathway in cancer: A comprehensive review
journal: Bosnian Journal of Basic Medical Sciences
why: Comprehensive cancer-application review (basal cell carcinoma, medulloblastoma, pancreatic/gastric cancer, smoothened-inhibitor resistance); anchors disease-association and drug-resistance edges absent from the mechanism-only papers currently in corpus.
authors: Skoda AM, Simovic D, Karin V, Kardum V, Vranic S, Serman L.

title: The Hippo pathway: regulators and regulations
why: Focused review of the core MST1/2-SAV1-LATS1/2-MOB1 kinase cascade and its upstream regulators; anchors the kinase-cascade edge structure that meng2016 (regulation mechanisms) and dupont2011/zanconato2015 (downstream YAP/TAZ output) do not detail at the kinase level.
authors: Yu FX, Guan KL.

title: Mechanobiology of YAP and TAZ in physiology and disease
why: Comprehensive review of mechanical inputs (ECM stiffness, cell shape, cytoskeletal tension) that regulate YAP/TAZ independent of the core kinase cascade; anchors upstream mechanosensing edges that dupont2011 only introduces and the corpus otherwise lacks.
authors: Panciera T, Azzolin L, Cordenonsi M, Piccolo S.

title: Force Triggers YAP Nuclear Entry by Regulating Transport across Nuclear Pores
why: Primary mechanistic paper showing cytoskeletal force directly stretches nuclear pores to permit YAP nuclear entry, independent of LATS phosphorylation; anchors a distinct, molecularly specific mechanosensing edge (nuclear-pore mechanics) complementing the Panciera review above.
authors: Elosegui-Artola A, Andreu I, Beedle AEM, Lezamiz A, Uroz M, Kosmalska AJ, Oria R, Kechagia JZ, Rico-Lastres P, Le Roux AL, Shanahan CM, Trepat X, Navajas D, Garcia-Manyes S, Roca-Cusachs P.

title: The Hippo-YAP pathway in organ size control and tumorigenesis: an updated version
why: Cornerstone review linking Hippo-YAP activity to organ-size control (via cell proliferation/apoptosis balance) and tumorigenesis; anchors the organ-size-control and tumor-suppressor-network edges that zanconato2015 (enhancer-level) and meng2016 do not address at the tissue/organism level.
authors: Zhao B, Li L, Lei Q, Guan KL.

title: Sestrin2 is a leucine sensor for the mTORC1 pathway
why: Primary mechanistic paper identifying Sestrin2 as a direct leucine-binding sensor that regulates GATOR2/Rag-GTPase signaling to mTORC1; anchors the specific amino-acid-sensor node upstream of the lysosomal recruitment step that sancak2010 (already in corpus) covers.
authors: Wolfson RL, Chantranupong L, Saxton RA, Shen K, Scaria SM, Cantor JR, Sabatini DM.

title: A Tumor Suppressor Complex with GAP Activity for the Rag GTPases That Signal Amino Acid Sufficiency to mTORC1
why: Identifies the GATOR1 complex (DEPDC5-NPRL2-NPRL3) as the GTPase-activating protein that shuts off Rag/mTORC1 signaling under amino-acid starvation; anchors a distinct upstream negative-regulator node/edge complementary to Sestrin2 and to sancak2010's lysosomal recruitment mechanism.
authors: Bar-Peled L, Chantranupong L, Cherniack AD, Chen WW, Ottina KA, Grabiner BC, Spear ED, Carter SL, Meyerson M, Sabatini DM.

title: SAMTOR is an S-adenosylmethionine sensor for the mTORC1 pathway
why: Identifies SAMTOR as a direct sensor of methionine availability (via S-adenosylmethionine) acting on the GATOR1/KICSTOR axis; adds a third, molecularly distinct nutrient-sensor node (methionine, alongside leucine/Sestrin2 and general amino-acid sufficiency/GATOR1) to the mTORC1 sensing network.
authors: Gu X, Orozco JM, Saxton RA, Saxton RA, Condon KJ, Liu GY, Krawczyk PA, Scaria SM, Harper JW, Gygi SP, Sabatini DM.

title: mTOR Signaling in Growth Control and Disease
why: Cornerstone comprehensive review (Laplante & Sabatini) of mTORC1/mTORC2 composition, growth-control outputs (protein/lipid/nucleotide synthesis), and disease links (cancer, diabetes, aging); the single most-cited mTOR review and a natural hub node distinct from the narrower liu2020/szwed2021 papers already in corpus.
authors: Laplante M, Sabatini DM.

title: AMPK and mTOR regulate autophagy through direct phosphorylation of Ulk1
why: Primary mechanistic paper showing mTORC1 and AMPK directly and antagonistically phosphorylate ULK1 to switch autophagy off/on; anchors the specific mTOR-autophagy crosstalk edge (mTORC1-to-ULK1) that mizushima2008 (already in corpus, general autophagy review) does not cover mechanistically.
authors: Kim J, Kundu M, Viollet B, Guan KL.

title: Activation mechanism of the insulin receptor revealed by cryo-EM structure of the fully liganded receptor-ligand complex
why: The corpus insulin-receptor entry (haeusler2018) is a biochemical review with no structural companion, unlike EGFR (zhang2006) and FGFR (schlessinger2000). This cryo-EM paper resolves the full ligand-induced conformational transition of the insulin receptor, adding a receptor-activation-mechanism node type absent for this receptor family.
authors: Uchikawa E, Choi E, Shang G, Yu H, Bai XC.

title: Structural basis of the activation of c-MET receptor
why: Adds an entirely new RTK subfamily: c-MET/HGF is a major oncology target with no representative paper among the current 8 RTK entries (all ErbB/EGFR, FGFR, or insulin receptor). Provides the cryo-EM structure of full-length MET bound to HGF, giving a distinct receptor-ligand activation mechanism (2:2 HGF-MET complex) not covered by the ErbB-centric structural entries already present.
authors: Uchikawa E, Chen Z, Xiao GY, Zhang X, Bai XC.

title: Resistance mechanisms to osimertinib in EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer
why: The corpus has deep ErbB mechanistic coverage (yarden2001, zhang2006, jones2006) but nothing on clinical RTK-inhibitor resistance, a major disease/therapeutic angle. This review catalogs on-target (C797S) and off-target (MET amplification, HER2 amplification, bypass RTK activation) resistance mechanisms to a first-line EGFR-TKI, adding a drug-resistance edge type linking RTK mutation status to clinical outcome.
authors: Leonetti A, Sharma S, Minari R, Perego P, Giovannetti E, Tiseo M.

title: Structural basis for chemokine recognition and receptor activation of chemokine receptor CCR5
why: The existing GPCR corpus is broad/mechanistic (activation, arrestin coupling, biased signaling) but has no receptor-family-specific structural entry beyond the beta2-adrenergic receptor (rasmussen2011). CCR5 is a major chemokine GPCR (HIV co-receptor, immune signaling) with a cryo-EM structure showing chemokine N-terminus insertion into the orthosteric pocket, a distinct receptor-class/ligand-recognition mechanism from the class-A aminergic receptor already represented.
authors: Zhang H, Chen K, Tan Q, Shao Q, Han S, Zhang C, Yi C, Chu X, Zhu Y, Xu Y, Zhao Q, Wu B.

title: Structural insights into mu-opioid receptor activation
why: A landmark GPCR structural biology paper (880+ citations) resolving the active-state mu-opioid receptor bound to a G-protein-mimetic nanobody, foundational to the field's understanding of the conserved GPCR activation switch. The corpus's weis2018 review discusses this mechanism narratively but has no structural anchor paper for an opioid/analgesia-relevant receptor. Fills both a structural-depth gap and a major therapeutic-relevance gap.
authors: Huang W, Manglik A, Venkatakrishnan AJ, Laeremans T, Feinberg EN, Sanborn AL, Kato HE, Livingston KE, Thorsen TS, Kling RC, Granier S, Gmeiner P, Husbands SM, Traynor JR, Weis WI, Steyaert J, Dror RO, Kobilka BK.

title: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs): advances in structures, mechanisms and drug discovery
why: Synthesizes the cryo-EM-era explosion of GPCR structures (2019-2024) that postdates every existing GPCR review in the corpus (weis2018 predates cryo-EM's routine application to GPCRs; smith2018 focuses narrowly on biased signaling).
